scenarios.context: Two classmates prepare for a presentation.

speakerA.en: Are you ready for the presentation tomorrow, Sara?
Don't worry. You know the topic well. Have you practised it?
Try looking at the back wall and speak slowly. I can listen to you tonight if you want.
Of course. And remember to smile. It helps everyone relax.

speakerB.en: Not really. I'm nervous because I have to speak in front of the whole class.
Twice. But I forget my words when I look at people.
That would be great. Could you tell me if I speak too fast?
Thanks, Sara. I already feel more confident.

scenarios.context: Two classmates decide when and where to work on a project.

speakerA.en: Our science project is due next Friday. When can we meet?
Tuesday is fine for me. Where should we work, the library or someone's house?
Okay. Let's decide who does what. I can make the poster and find the pictures.
Sure. I'll message him tonight and send everyone the time.

speakerB.en: I have football practice on Monday and Wednesday. How about Tuesday after school?
The library is quieter, but we can't talk much there. Let's go to my house.
I'll write the report. Could you ask Ali to prepare the presentation?
Perfect. Please remind everyone to bring their notes.

scenarios.context: A student apologizes after being late and rude in class.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, Mrs. Brown. Do you have a minute?
I'm sorry I was late and talked during the lesson yesterday. It was rude of me.
My bus broke down, but I should have called the school. It won't happen again.
I will. Can I do anything to make up for the lesson I missed?

speakerB.en: Of course. What's the matter?
Thank you for telling me. Why were you late?
I understand. Next time, send a message, and I'll know you are safe.
Just read page forty and ask me tomorrow if you have any questions.

scenarios.context: Two friends talk about their maths test results.

speakerA.en: Did you get your maths test result? I'm a little worried about mine.
That's excellent! I only got twelve. I made silly mistakes in the last questions.
I know, but my parents expect more. I'm afraid to show them the paper.
Really? That would help me a lot. Which topics are difficult for you?

speakerB.en: Yes, I got seventeen out of twenty. I was surprised because I didn't study much.
Don't be upset. Twelve isn't bad, and you can improve it next time.
Just be honest and tell them your plan. Maybe you can study with me at weekends.
Fractions were hard at first. We can practise them together and check each other's answers.

scenarios.context: A mother and her daughter talk about new classes at school.

speakerA.en: Mum, our school offers new after-school classes. I want to join one.
There's a drawing class, a robotics club and an English conversation course.
I like robotics, but English will help me in the future, too.
Good point. I'll take English on Sundays and ask my teacher about robotics later.

speakerB.en: That's a good idea. What are your choices?
They all sound useful. Which one are you most interested in?
Why not choose English now and try robotics next term? It's better not to do too much.
Great. Let's register online tonight before the places are full.
